probe.caveat: These observations were measured on the previous round's isolated engine, not on the acceptance database, and only for the four identities this seed did not create (the elementary carbon dioxide row, the two hydrogen seed catalog flows and the two unit groups). The install validation step must re-run the same read-only probes against the target engine and store both readings in the install receipt; a changed row is a blocking finding, not a warning. No catalog probe exists for any of the fourteen seed owned rows.

elementary_identity_resolution.scope: every biosphere port of this seed, resolved as an exact dataset version identity rather than an emission factor
elementary_identity_resolution.caveat: GET /api/reference/flows/{flow_uuid} carries no version identity for elementary flows: source_namespace, version_label and tidas_flow_property_uuid all read null there, so a probe through that endpoint can neither prove nor disprove a pin. The provider catalog resolver is the only public endpoint that returns exact elementary Flow version identity, and the installer must re-call it read-only at the verified stage of every install.

technosphere_identity.contract: docs/STANDARD_LCA_SEED_PACKAGE_V1.md section 5.2. Every type == technosphere port of model/graph.json must carry the flow property pair and the unit group pair of its own basis, and the builder compares the port against this block rather than against any constant of its own.
technosphere_identity.why: Nebula One submits the graph as an inline_snapshot, so the engine judges each technosphere flow from the request body alone: an incomplete port identity is a 422 CUSTOM_TECHNOSPHERE_IDENTITY_INCOMPLETE naming that exchange, and no amount of request-side reference carries the identity. A snapshot_ref solve of the same stored model returns 200 with the same nulls, so the gap stays invisible until the application layer runs it.

mass.provenance: POST /api/provider/v1/catalog/resolve flow_properties on the acceptance engine, status resolved, name_en Mass (runtime/seed-install-2026-09-18/evidence/segment9-slice5-1.2.0-01/flow-property-resolve-02.json)

electricity.read_as: the FlowProperty the exact Tiangong read-back recorded for the electricity flow

technosphere_identity.caveat: The engine's inline check only proves the four fields are present; it does not test whether a flow property matches its unit group, and the electricity property above cannot be named by the current engine, which answers FLOW_PROPERTY_RESOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for any exact-version Flow Property resource. So the two electricity ports carry a declared identity the builder checks for completeness and consistency, not one the engine has confirmed, and gap GS-04 records that.
